name: Sheela Foam Ltd
title: Sheela Foam Ltd - 540203 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q1 FY27 margin fell as raw-material volatility hit gross margin, but management leaned on foam volume and overseas gains; standalone volume only ~6% and no capacity discipline signal.

summary.headline: Sheela Foam Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 26% to INR1,032 crore and EBITDA 45% to INR109 crore, with margin at 10.6%.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 26% YoY to INR1,032 crore and EBITDA rose 45% to INR109 crore, with margin up 139 bps to 10.6%. Standalone India revenue grew 20% to INR761 crore and EBITDA 13% to INR68 crore, with gross margin compressed by sharp raw-material (TDI/polyol) swings that management attributes to the Middle East conflict. Management chose to keep growing foam volumes, which was cash-accretive, and international subsidiaries (Australia, Spain) posted sharply higher margins on inventory gains. Management reiterated a 15% EBITDA margin target for next year and expects volumes to recover in the festive quarters.

segments.name: India mattresses
segments.commentary: Value up 15% and volume up 6% YoY. U2O channel revenue up 81% with volume up 19%, now about 10,000 dealers, helped by 5- and 6-inch mattresses.

segments.name: India foam
segments.commentary: Value up 26% and volume up 4% YoY; faster foam growth diluted gross margin but was cash-accretive as competitors lacked raw material.

segments.name: E-commerce
segments.commentary: Brand.com sales up 69% YoY, platforms up 19%; overall category up 30% with volumes up 23%.

segments.name: Staqo (IT)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 67% YoY with EBITDA margin around 28-30%; Presence 360 crossed 3.2 lakh users.

segments.name: Furlenco (associate)
segments.commentary: Operating profit roughly INR9 crore per quarter; Q1 PAT share reflects 35% stake and no deferred tax asset recognition (DTA only booked at year end, likely Q4).

guidance_outlook: Reiterated 15% EBITDA margin target for next year; management said there is no change to this stance, though Rachna Kukreja's question suggested earlier 11-12% FY27 guidance.
Expects more than 15% revenue growth for the full year and double-digit volume growth in both foam and mattresses for FY27.

International operations to grow about 5% in local currency with 10-12% EBITDA margins; for FY27, management is confident of crossing INR1,000 crore revenue and about INR120 crore EBITDA for overseas operations.
Synergy benefit of about INR40 crore still pending; machine under installation, with full impact expected in Q3.
Integration of Kurlon about 96-97% complete; roughly 75-80% of synergies realised, with the balance expected.
Expects volume recovery with Q3 (festive) and Q4 the strongest quarters; FY27 volume expected to exceed last year.
Expects ROCE to reach roughly 20-25% in three years from about 10% currently.
Debt: India debt above INR300 crore to be cleared in about one year; overseas debt of about INR350 crore to be repaid over five years. Balance sheet will not be debt free by year-end.
capex_capacity: Company-operated stores (COCO): about INR27 lakh capex per store plus INR20-22 lakh working capital; about INR50 lakh per store, so about INR25 crore for 50 stores. Stores are about 2,000 sq ft (range 1,800-3,000).
COCO store rollout: 22 existing stores upgraded; target 50 stores with about 42 operational.
Furlenco shop-in-shop: about 40-50 stores currently; first target 100 stores. Company has about 3,500 exclusive brand outlets.
Standalone synergy-related machine under installation, expected to deliver full impact in Q3.
Operating units reduced from 21 to 12 as part of Kurlon integration.
demand_pricing: Standalone India volume growth about 6%; management views sub-10% as satisfactory and says industry grew close to 5%.
U2O price increase taken last year to fix channel margins; value growth well ahead of volume as a result; management says the pricing level is now sustainable.
Raw material (TDI/polyol) prices swung roughly +40% to -20% in the period; prices spiked in March after the Feb 28 Iran conflict, eased in April, then rose again about a month before the call.
Management says price increases pass through commensurately, but in-pipe inventory on the high seas can lag on sharp falls and hit margin.
Foam share of COGS: TDI and polyol are 65-70% of COGS.
Premiumisation: ASP marginally up across segments; new products introduced to lift ASP; consumer-led promotions launched.
Organised mattress market combined share of Sleepwell and Kurlon close to 20%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Australia/Spain margin gain sustainable, and how much of it is inventory benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the gains came from longer-held low-cost inventory and yield and supply chain programmes. Overseas momentum should moderate as India recovers, with normal inventory levels by Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone volume growth slow to single digits and margins fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to a price-volume trade-off after the steep price hikes, and expects double-digit volume growth for the year once volatility eases. Gross margins were hit mainly by foam, while incremental foam sales generated cash.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 15% EBITDA margin target and 13-14% FY28 guidance hold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has not guided for 13% for FY27 (only 11-12%) but stands by its margin commitment; the current volatility makes it hard to comment, and gross margin has fallen more than the guided range.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex and rollout of company-owned stores?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR27 lakh capex plus INR20-22 lakh working capital per store, with 42 operational of a 50-store target; about INR25 crore for another 50 COCO stores.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Kurlon integration status and synergy realisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Integration about 96-97% complete, operating units cut to 12 from 21, and roughly 75-80% of synergies realised, with the remainder on track.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Furlenco store rollout?
qa_highlights.answer: Furlenco is present in 40-50 shop-in-shop stores with a first target of 100, and will go only where it fits its micro-market strategy.

risks_watch: Raw material volatility: TDI/polyol (65-70% of COGS) swung roughly +40% to -20%; management expects volatility for at least a couple of months, possibly to October-November, so gross margin recovery timing is uncertain.

Margin target credibility: management reiterated 15% EBITDA margin for next year but declined to comment on the 12-13% FY27 and 13-14% FY28 figures put to it, saying volatility makes it hard to judge; gross margin fell more than the guided range.

Overseas margin sustainability: Australia and Spain margins (12.8% and 14.7%) were helped by longer-held low-cost inventory and lower frequency of price changes; management expects moderation as India recovers and inventory normalises by Q2.

Volume recovery: standalone India volume grew about 6% against double-digit growth last year; management expects double-digit volume growth for FY27 and strongest volumes in Q3 and Q4, contingent on volatility subsiding.

Synergy and capex execution: about INR40 crore synergy pending the machine installation (full impact expected Q3); COCO rollout of 50 stores at about INR50 lakh each (~INR25 crore) and Furlenco shop-in-shop target of 100 stores from about 40-50.

Balance sheet: India debt above INR300 crore to be cleared in about one year; overseas debt of about INR350 crore over five years; company will not be debt free by year-end despite INR150-200 crore cash generation.
key_quotes: For the first time in the group's history, Sheela Foam has reported a consolidated revenues of more than INR1,000 crores and EBITDA of more than INR100 crores in the first quarter of any fiscal year.
So, we guided for 11% to 12%. We never guided for 13% for the current year. Yes, we do stand for it.
There is no change in stand on the margins. We have a target of 15% EBITDA margin for the next year.
So, there would definitely be volume recovery. I would say we would go back higher than what the volumes we clocked last year.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on the quarter, the Kurlon integration and the medium-term targets, but cautious and non-committal on near-term margins, which it attributed to raw-material volatility. It declined to give a view on the 12-13% FY27 and 13-14% FY28 margin figures put to it and repeatedly said it would revisit once volatility eases.
